accepted_warns.why: 1.1 mm ledges round the M4 hole in the roof of the fin-to-tray nut slots (inboard halves); under the 3 mm limit. Layer map cad/review/a5_designer/fin_R_inboard_z019.0_cantilever.png
0.9 mm2 ledge where the rear leaf slot's corner meets the top-link cavity chamfer (slot widened for the r 2.0 root fillets); under the 3 mm limit
L-shaped roof at |x'| 20.1 (a7: the cartridge is 40 wide): the block pocket (11.7 wide) and the ground-bar pocket (7.2 wide), each closed on all sides; the number is the L's length, not a span

C-shaped roof at |x'| 21.1 (a7): the stop-screw flank slot, the drop cavity with the front leaf slot, the top-link cavity side, and the rear leaf slot with the catch slot, each closed on all sides; widest span 21 (drop + front leaf slot), the rest 14-16. The number is the outline's length, not a span

fin halves: 1.3 mm webs behind the cartridge block (between the block pocket at y 46.4 and the cell's wire-boss pocket at 47.7, below the cell): the fin's lip for the block, by design; carries the pull reaction in bearing, not bending

as the inboard halves (1.3 mm web behind the block); and the sloped overhang is the cell-pocket and flank teardrop flanks and the 45 deg lead-relief roof (all 45 deg nominal, read 44.x on facets), plus the fin's 39 deg reveal on the bed edge

cartridges: 0.86 mm between the pull screw's clearance hole behind its nut and the link's 45 deg chamfer (no load across it), the r 2 root fillets' thin tips, and 159 mm2 of overhang = the upper 60 deg faces of the four M3 nut pockets (corners up, 3.2 mm faces) plus the 45 deg teardrop flanks; layer check: max bridge 5.7, max ledge 1.0, no cantilever

every face steeper than 45 deg (steep_strip.py on the STL, 813-875 mm2) is a strip at print z 0-5 that starts on the bed: the front-bottom chamfer, the bed-edge flanks of the rear slope and the centre-seam V reveal where it meets the bed (46-54 deg from vertical); boss undersides read 44.7-44.9 on facets. Walls 1.0-1.5 where the reveal crosses the chamfered front bottom edge. Printcheck: max bridge 2.8, max ledge 0.9
as L (no RJ45 pad)
the lead is modelled from the boss axis; its first 15 mm is the cell's own boss
as R
jumper ends modelled at the header pin centres
ESP32 screws by the tray's front wall: the drill body needs to be above the wall, so a 150 mm 1/4 in hex extension (README tools); done on the bench before the tray goes on
as screw 2
designed: 150 mm 1/4 in hex extension + 4 mm hex bit through the Ø14 hole in the tray floor along the bolt axis (reviewer a2 #9 fix); no L-key
as bolt 4

accepted_warns.match: head stands 15.0 mm off the part
accepted_warns.why: push stop screws: by design the head's TOP face is the stop (it meets the counterbore floor in the block when the link moves forward); the shank crosses the 15 mm gap beside the cell to its nut in the link and is never clamped

bench jack: the M5 x 35 head floats 9.1 mm (bench_standoff) behind the cradle's rear upright, so the screw travels both ways and the jack nut + the 3.5 mm mass hanger fit under it for the known-mass check (the checker measures to the hanger, parked on the shank); the push stroke needed is cradle_stroke (stacks row)

accepted_warns.match: FST_Jack_swivel_nut has no bolt on its axis
accepted_warns.why: the second nut on the jack screw: glued on its tip as the swivel in the setting plug's T-slot; the checker pairs each bolt with one nut (the upright's)
bench cradle (attempt 6 closed frame): the 45 deg teardrop flanks of the lip-screw holes, the corner-up hex nut pockets and the lead notches; printcheck max bridge 4.1, max ledge 0.7
by design: the lip screw's shank inside the cradle is the lip behind the cartridge's block (the pull reaction, as the fin's lip)

a7: 1.1-1.8 mm ledges (all under 1 mm2 or 9 mm2, under the 3 mm limit): the tray's rear fin-bolt boss (moved to y 141, z -18) meeting the 45 deg rear-wall boss and its M4 counterbore; the fin's lower M4 nut slot roof (110, -56); the corner where the swept boss pocket meets the cell pocket. printcheck on the STLs agrees (warn, 0 fail)
